zh:
禪波羅蜜序
《禪波羅蜜》者，《輔行》云：「《次第禪門》，《目錄》云：大師於瓦官寺說也，大莊嚴寺法慎私記，章安頂禪師治定為十卷。開十大章：一、大意；二、釋名；三、明門；四、詮次；五、法心；六、方便；七、修證；八、果報；九、起教；十、歸趣。但至修證，餘三略無。於修證中，又開四別：一、世間禪；二、亦世間亦出世間；三、出世間；四、非世間非出世間。四中唯至第三、出世，復為二：一、對治無漏；二、緣理無漏。但至對治，又為九，謂九想、八念、十想、背捨、勝處、一切處、九次第定、奮迅、超越。然修證之相，豈可盡具？傳曰：『大師甞在高座云：若說《次第禪門》，年可一遍；若著章疏，可五十卷。』」今刊預示大科，庶學者不昧始末云。
en:
Preface to the Dhyāna-Pāramitā
As for the Dhyāna-Pāramitā, the Fuxing says: "The Sequential Gates of Dhyāna — the Catalog says: the Great Master spoke it at Waguan Temple; Fashen of Great Adornment Temple recorded it privately; Chan Master [Guan]ding of Zhang'an settled it into ten fascicles. It opens into ten great chapters: first, the great intent; second, explaining the name; third, clarifying the gates; fourth, the sequence of exposition; fifth, dharma and mind; sixth, expedient means; seventh, cultivation and realization; eighth, fruits and rewards; ninth, the arising of teaching; tenth, the ultimate destination. But it reaches only as far as cultivation and realization; the remaining three are omitted. Within cultivation and realization there is a further fourfold division: first, worldly dhyāna; second, dhyāna both worldly and world-transcending; third, world-transcending dhyāna; fourth, dhyāna neither worldly nor world-transcending. Of these four, it reaches only the third, the world-transcending, which divides again into two: first, the uncontaminated that counteracts affliction; second, the uncontaminated that takes principle as its object. It reaches only the counteracting, which divides again into nine: namely, the nine contemplations, the eight recollections, the ten contemplations, the liberations, the stations of mastery, the totality-bases, the nine sequential concentrations, the lion's-sport, and transcendence. Yet how could the marks of cultivation and realization ever be set out in full? It is handed down: 'The Great Master once said from the high seat: If I were to speak the Sequential Gates of Dhyāna, it would take about a year to go through once; if I were to write it up as a commentary, it might run to fifty fascicles.'" In printing it now, the overall outline is shown in advance, so that students may not be left in the dark about its beginning and end.

en:
The Ten Great Chapters
1. The great intent of cultivating dhyāna-pāramitā (fascicle 1, upper and lower parts)
2. Explaining the name of dhyāna-pāramitā
3. Clarifying the gates of dhyāna-pāramitā
4. Distinguishing the sequence in which dhyāna-pāramitā is explained
5. Discriminating the dharma and mind of dhyāna-pāramitā
6. Distinguishing the preliminary expedient means of dhyāna-pāramitā, in two parts
　(1) The external expedient means (fascicle 2)
　(2) The internal expedient means, in two parts
　　(a) Rightly clarifying how inner and outer wholesome roots arise through stopping (fascicle 3, upper and lower parts)
　　(b) Verifying unwholesome capacity (fascicle 4)
7. Explaining the cultivation and realization of dhyāna-pāramitā, in four parts
　(1) The marks of cultivating and realizing worldly dhyāna, in three parts
　　(a) The four dhyānas (fascicle 5)
　　(b) The four immeasurable minds (fascicle 6)
　　(c) The four formless concentrations
　(2) The marks of cultivating and realizing dhyāna both worldly and world-transcending, in three parts
　　(a) The six wondrous gates (fascicle 7)
　　(b) The sixteen special excellences
　　(c) The thorough-and-bright contemplation (fascicle 8)
　(3) The marks of cultivating and realizing world-transcending dhyāna, in two parts
　　(a) The uncontaminated that counteracts affliction, in nine
　　　Observing — the destructible-dharma path (fascicle 9)
　　　　i. The nine contemplations
　　　　ii. The eight recollections
　　　　iii. The ten contemplations
　　　Observing — the indestructible-dharma path (fascicle 10)
　　　　iv. The eight liberations
　　　　v. The eight stations of mastery
　　　　vi. The ten totality-bases
　　　Refining
　　　　vii. The nine sequential concentrations
　　　Perfuming
　　　　viii. The lion's-sport samādhi
　　　Mastering
　　　　ix. The transcendence samādhi
　　(b) The uncontaminated that takes principle as its object (not discussed)
　(4) The marks of cultivating and realizing dhyāna neither worldly nor world-transcending
8. Revealing the fruits and rewards of dhyāna-pāramitā
9. The teachings that arise from dhyāna-pāramitā
10. Gathering together and returning to where dhyāna-pāramitā ultimately leads

zh:
卷第一之上
隋天台智者大師說
弟子法慎記
弟子灌頂再治
en:
Fascicle One, Upper Part
Spoken by the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai, of the Sui dynasty
Recorded by his disciple Fashen
Revised and edited by his disciple Guanding

zh: （天台山修禪寺顗禪師於都講說禪法，大莊嚴寺沙門法慎記。預聽學輒依說採記。法門深廣，難可委悉，若取具足，有三十卷，今略出前卷要用，流通此本，於天台更得治改前諸同學所寫之者。爾時既未好成就，猶應闕略，或繁而不次，若見此本，更改定之，庶於學者得免謬失矣）。
en: (Chan Master [Zhi]yi of Xiuchan Temple on Mount Tiantai expounded the Dharma of dhyāna in the lecture assembly, and the śramaṇa Fashen of Great Adornment Temple recorded it. Those who attended as students took notes as it was spoken. The dharma-gates are deep and vast, hard to record in every detail; taken in full, they would run to thirty fascicles. Here the essentials of the earlier fascicles are briefly drawn out and this copy is circulated; on Tiantai it was further possible to revise what fellow students had copied earlier. Since at that time it was not yet well finished, there are bound still to be gaps and omissions, or passages that are prolix and out of order. Whoever sees this copy should revise and settle it further, so that students may be spared errors.)

zh: 《釋禪波羅蜜次第法門》，大開為十意不同。所言十意者：修禪波羅蜜大意第一，釋禪波羅蜜名第二，明禪波羅蜜門第三，辨禪波羅蜜詮次第四，簡禪波羅蜜法心第五，分別禪波羅蜜前方便第六，釋禪波羅蜜修證第七，顯示禪波羅蜜果報第八，從禪波羅蜜起教第九，結會禪波羅蜜歸趣第十。
en: This treatise, Explaining the Sequential Dharma-Gates of Dhyāna-Pāramitā, opens broadly into ten distinct topics. The ten topics are: first, the great intent of cultivating dhyāna-pāramitā; second, explaining the name of dhyāna-pāramitā; third, clarifying the gates of dhyāna-pāramitā; fourth, distinguishing the sequence in which dhyāna-pāramitā is explained; fifth, discriminating the dharma and mind of dhyāna-pāramitā; sixth, distinguishing the preliminary expedient means of dhyāna-pāramitā; seventh, explaining the cultivation and realization of dhyāna-pāramitā; eighth, revealing the fruits and rewards of dhyāna-pāramitā; ninth, the teachings that arise from dhyāna-pāramitā; and tenth, gathering together and returning to where dhyāna-pāramitā ultimately leads.

zh: 今約此十義以辨禪波羅蜜者，文則略收諸佛教法之始終，理則遠通如來之祕藏。一切圓妙法界，若教若行，若事若理，始從凡夫，終至極聖，所有因、果、行、位悉在其中。若行人深達禪門意趣，則自然解了一切佛法，不俟餘尋。故《摩訶衍》云：「譬如牽衣一角，則眾處皆動。」
en: To treat dhyāna-pāramitā by means of these ten topics is, in its written form, to gather in outline the whole beginning and end of every buddha's teaching; in its principle, it reaches far into the hidden treasury of the Tathāgata himself. The entire perfect and wondrous dharma-realm — every teaching and every practice, every phenomenon and every principle, from the ordinary person at the very start to the ultimate sage at the very end — with every cause, fruit, practice, and stage, is contained within it. If a practitioner penetrates deeply into the intent of these gates of dhyāna, they will naturally come to understand the whole of the Buddhadharma, with no need to search further. Hence the Mahāyāna treatise says: "It is like tugging at one corner of a garment — every part of it moves."

zh: 所以第一先明修禪波羅蜜大意者，菩薩發心，所為正求菩提淨妙之法，必須簡擇真偽，善識祕要。若欲具足一切諸佛法藏，唯禪為最。如得珠玉，眾寶皆獲。是故發意修禪。既欲修習，應知名字，尋名取理，其義不虛。以釋禪名，尋名求理，理則非門不通。次明禪門。
en: This is why the first topic explains, first of all, the great intent of cultivating dhyāna-pāramitā: when a bodhisattva sets the mind on the pure and wondrous Dharma of bodhi, they must discriminate the true from the false, and skillfully recognize what is essential. If one wishes to be complete in the entire treasury of every buddha's Dharma, dhyāna alone is foremost — like obtaining a single pearl through which every other treasure is gained at once. This is why the mind is first set on cultivating dhyāna. Having resolved to cultivate it, one should know its name; by tracing the name one grasps the principle, and the meaning is not empty. Hence the name "dhyāna" is explained — tracing the name to seek the principle, and the principle cannot be entered except through its gate. Next, then, the gates of dhyāna are clarified.

zh: 禪定幽遠，無由頓入，必須從淺至深，故應辯詮次。夫欲涉淺遊深，復當善識禪中境智，是以次簡法心。既明識法心，若欲習行，事須善巧，次分別方便。依法而行，必有所證，次釋修證。若得內心相應，因成則感果，次顯示果報。從因至果，自行既圓，便樹立益物之功，次釋教門。理教既已圓備，法相同歸平等一實之道，次結會指歸。
en: Since dhyāna-concentration is deep and far-reaching, it cannot be entered all at once; one must proceed from the shallow to the deep, and so the order of its exposition must be distinguished. And in order to wade from the shallows into the depths, one must also skillfully recognize the objects and the wisdom at work within dhyāna — hence dharma and mind are next discriminated. Once dharma and mind are clearly recognized, if one wishes to put it into practice, skillful means are needed — hence the preliminary expedient means are next distinguished. Practicing in accordance with the Dharma, one is certain to attain realization — hence cultivation and realization are next explained. Once inner accord is attained, the cause, once complete, brings forth its fruit — hence the fruits and rewards are next revealed. Once the practice for oneself, from cause to fruit, is complete, one then establishes the work of benefiting others — hence the gate of teaching is next explained. Once both principle and teaching are complete, all dharma-characteristics return alike to the one real way of equality — hence the topics are last gathered together and their destination pointed out.

zh: 以此十義相生，辯釋禪波羅蜜，總攝一切眾行法門。至下尋文，泠然可見。故《大品經》云：「菩薩從初已來，住禪波羅蜜中，具足修一切佛法，乃至坐道場，成一切種智，起轉法輪，是名菩薩次第行、次第學、次第道。」
en: By these ten topics, arising one from another, dhyāna-pāramitā is analyzed and explained, gathering together every dharma-gate of practice as a whole. As the text is followed further below, this will become clear of itself. Hence the Larger Sūtra says: "From the very beginning, the bodhisattva abides within dhyāna-pāramitā, cultivating the entire Buddhadharma in full, until at last sitting at the seat of enlightenment, accomplishing the wisdom that knows all things in every mode, and turning the wheel of the Dharma. This is called the bodhisattva's sequential practice, sequential study, sequential path."

This opening sets the whole treatise's method: ten topics, each one generating the need for the next, so that the order of exposition is itself an argument, not just a table of contents. The chain runs from motivation (why cultivate dhyāna at all) through name, gates, sequence, and mental states, into actual practice — expedient means, cultivation, realization, fruit — and out again into teaching others and, finally, the single "real way of equality" everything was always pointing toward. Ru-Yi's translation follows this same sequence fascicle by fascicle; see the translation notes for how key terms here — dhyāna-pāramitā, the "Mahāyāna treatise," the "Larger Sūtra" — are rendered consistently going forward.

quiz.q: According to the opening attribution, who spoke this treatise, who recorded it, and who revised it?
options: spoken by Zhiyi, recorded by Fashen, revised by Guanding
spoken by Zhiyi, recorded by Guanding, revised by Fashen
spoken by Huisi, recorded by Zhiyi, revised by Guanding
spoken by Guanding, recorded by Fashen, revised by Zhiyi
quiz.why: The opening attribution reads "Spoken by the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai, of the Sui dynasty; Recorded by his disciple Fashen; Revised and edited by his disciple Guanding." The treatise was spoken by Zhiyi, written down by Fashen, and revised by Guanding; the roles cannot be swapped, and Huisi, Zhiyi's own teacher, does not appear in the attribution.

quiz.q: Among the ten topics, what is the fifth?
options: clarifying the gates of dhyāna-pāramitā
discriminating the states of mind proper to dhyāna-pāramitā's method
distinguishing the sequence in which dhyāna-pāramitā is explained
distinguishing the preliminary expedient means of dhyāna-pāramitā
quiz.why: The text lists "fifth, discriminating the states of mind proper to dhyāna-pāramitā's method." Distinguishing the sequence is the fourth topic, clarifying the gates the third, and the preliminary expedient means the sixth.

quiz.q: The text quotes the Mahāyāna treatise: "It is like tugging at one corner of a garment — every part of it moves." What is this meant to show?
options: one who penetrates deeply into the intent of the gates of dhyāna naturally understands the whole Buddhadharma, with no need to search further
when the body moves during meditation, the mind scatters with it
the Dharma is too vast, so one corner is enough and completeness need not be sought
the ten topics must be practiced one at a time, never mixed
quiz.why: "If a practitioner penetrates deeply into the intent of these gates of dhyāna, they will naturally come to understand the whole of the Buddhadharma, with no need to search further." The corner of the garment stands for the gates of dhyāna and the whole garment for the entire Buddhadharma. The simile is not about bodily movement scattering the mind, nor does it say one corner is enough.

quiz.q: What does "like obtaining a single pearl through which every other treasure is gained at once" illustrate?
options: cultivating dhyāna brings worldly wealth
to be complete in the entire treasury of every buddha's Dharma, dhyāna alone is foremost
when precepts are pure, concentration comes by itself
giving is the highest of the six perfections
quiz.why: "If one wishes to be complete in the entire treasury of every buddha's Dharma, dhyāna alone is foremost — like obtaining a single pearl through which every other treasure is gained at once." The pearl is dhyāna; the other treasures are the whole Buddhadharma. It explains why the ten topics begin with the intent of cultivating dhyāna; it says nothing of worldly wealth, and it is not praising giving or precepts.

quiz.q: In the chain of the ten topics, why does the teaching that arises from dhyāna come right after the fruits and rewards?
options: once one's own practice from cause to fruit is complete, one establishes the work of benefiting others
once principle and teaching are complete, all dharma-characteristics return to the one real way
because the fruits are poor, a new teaching is needed to repair them
practicing in accordance with the Dharma, one is certain to attain realization
quiz.why: "Once the practice for oneself, from cause to fruit, is complete, one then establishes the work of benefiting others — hence the gate of teaching is next explained." The completion of principle and teaching is the reason for the tenth topic, and "practicing in accordance with the Dharma, one is certain to attain realization" is the reason for the seventh.
